ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: inventory-service: p99 latency above 1000ms for 5 minutes (since 15:43 UTC)
Alerting service: inventory
Alert time: 2026-07-12T15:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-07-12T14:00:00Z to 2026-07-12T17:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 4 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-07-12T16:00:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-07-12T15:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check latency progression for inventory service)
  Result: M-024: Change detected at 2026-07-12T15:45:00Z: mean 454.89 before, 3336.13 after (6.3 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-024] inventory.latency_p99_ms from 2026-07-12T15:30:00Z to 2026-07-12T16:00:00Z (7 points, 5-minute steps): min=128.94 max=4077.41 mean=2101.31 last=4075.52; mean=2101.31. Change detected at 2026-07-12T15:45:00Z: mean 454.89 before, 3336.13 after (6.3 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-07-12T15:30:00Z = 128.94 (lowest); 2026-07-12T15:45:00Z = 2101.29 (first point after the change); 2026-07-12T15:55:00Z = 4077.41 (peak); 2026-07-12T16:00:00Z = 4075.52 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-07-12T16:00:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-07-12T15:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check database connection pool usage for inventory service)
  Result: M-021: Change detected at 2026-07-12T15:45:00Z: mean 35.65 before, 77.43 after (5.9 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-021] inventory.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-07-12T15:30:00Z to 2026-07-12T16:00:00Z (7 points, 5-minute steps): min=27.7 max=89.12 mean=59.53 last=85.74; mean=59.53. Change detected at 2026-07-12T15:45:00Z: mean 35.65 before, 77.43 after (5.9 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-07-12T15:35:00Z = 27.7 (lowest); 2026-07-12T15:45:00Z = 61.28 (first point after the change); 2026-07-12T15:55:00Z = 89.12 (peak); 2026-07-12T16:00:00Z = 85.74 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-07-12T15:45:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "query": "slow database timeout error", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-07-12T15:40:00Z"} (asked because: Look for database or timeout errors in inventory logs around the alert time)
  Result: 0 matching log lines.
Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-07-12T16:00:00Z", "metric": "cache_hit_ratio_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-07-12T15:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check if cache hit ratio dropped, pointing to cache stampede or cache outage.)
  Result: M-019: Only 7 points in this range, too few to test for a change; use a wider range.
  [M-019] inventory.cache_hit_ratio_pct from 2026-07-12T15:30:00Z to 2026-07-12T16:00:00Z (7 points, 5-minute steps): min=0 max=93.74 mean=26.55 last=0; mean=26.55. Only 7 points in this range, too few to test for a change; use a wider range. Notable points: 2026-07-12T15:30:00Z = 93.74 (peak); 2026-07-12T15:40:00Z = 0 (lowest); 2026-07-12T16:00:00Z = 0 (last).
Step 5: log_search {"end": "2026-07-12T16:00:00Z", "level": "WARN", "query": "slow query pool connection timeout", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-07-12T15:40:00Z"} (asked because: Search for slow query or connection pool warnings in inventory logs around the incident time.)
  Result: 1 matching log lines.
  [L-0310] 2026-07-12T15:53:37Z inventory WARN slow request took 588ms path=/api/v1/stock/bulk
Step 6: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "Database connection pool exhaustion or slow query missing index mitigation"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook instructions for database connection pool issues and slow queries.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-03-2 (similarity 0.77).
  [R-03-2] Slow query or missing index - Symptoms (similarity 0.77): Latency climbs and errors follow as requests wait on the database and time out. Logs mention database timeouts and slow queries. The connection pool may fill as a side effect, because every connection is busy running the slow statement for longer than usual.
  [R-03-8] Slow query or missing index - Related runbooks (similarity 0.72): If queries are quick but requests wait for connections, use the pool exhaustion runbook. If the database is overloaded because the cache failed, use the cache runbook. If pool use rises slowly over days instead, use the connection leak audit.
  [R-02-8] Database connection pool exhaustion - Related runbooks (similarity 0.70): If one query is simply taking seconds, use the slow query runbook. If pool use rises slowly over days, use the connection leak audit. If a cache failed first, use the cache runbook.

Previous hypotheses:
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: Database connection pool usage spiked significantly starting at 15:45 UTC, directly aligning with the sharp increase in service p99 latency. (evidence: M-024, M-021)
- slow_query_missing_index: High p99 latency accompanied by elevated database connection pool usage can be driven by slow-running queries holding connections open longer than usual. (evidence: M-024, M-021)
- cache_stampede_outage: A cache failure could cause a sudden surge of queries hitting the database, exhausting the connection pool and increasing latency. (evidence: M-024, M-021)
